checks.evidence: rules=['boundary-derived profile repair', 'deterministic mapping', 'operation-level rank features', 'profile-spec stack depth and predicates', 'supervised boundary-derived fields']
Rules choose profile knobs and guardrails rather than a label-free automatic selector.
All decisions derive operation fields or choose operation-stack queries; no third profiler object is introduced.
The script reads tracked R325/R358/R366 artifacts only.

claim: Operation-field derivation is actionable when the profiler can name a guarded configuration knob: mapping for compression, stack depth for view control, rank features for task-specific ordering, and boundary-derived fields only after suitability checks beat simple baselines.

decision_rules.avoid_when: the task needs fine action-boundary fidelity
decision_rules.counterpoint: It deliberately coarsens action labels: action->phase V-measure 0.9343->0.7416 and adjacent phase/action boundary F1 0.9677->0.7774. Mean task/dataset V-measure is unchanged at 0.7778; some datasets are already well structured and do not benefit.
decision_rules.evidence: Held-out mapping over 3990 operations reduces unique stacks 284->209 and improves compression 14.049->19.091; dataset->task V-measure 0.8374->0.8531. Across 9 held-out datasets / 13265 operations, mapped stacks reduce stack count on 6/9 datasets, never increase it (0 negative), and yield 1162.005 weighted stack reduction per 1k ops.
decision_rules.use_when: the goal is cross-dataset semantic aggregation or stack compression

decision_rules.avoid_when: a single default stack is being treated as universally optimal
decision_rules.counterpoint: Depth is objective-dependent: 3/6 tasks choose different stack depths for AP and first-positive work.
decision_rules.evidence: 12 profile-spec variants compose operation files, predicates, operation rank rules, rule-score ranking, and explicit stack depth; 12/12 are prompt/session-frame free. AP improves versus width in 9/12 variants and first-positive work in 10/12.
decision_rules.use_when: the same operation source must be folded into task-specific views

decision_rules.avoid_when: a feature is known to be misleading for the task family
decision_rules.counterpoint: 3 misleading feature rows: It also finds 3 misleading feature rows, including OSWorld input-phase and SATraj loop-like cases.
decision_rules.evidence: 7 critical feature rows: Leave-one-feature ablation identifies 7 critical feature rows across safety, looping, side-effect, and step-quality tasks. Examples include success, loop-like, write-action, and failure fields.
decision_rules.use_when: feature ablations identify task-specific positive signals

decision_rules.avoid_when: a simple visible field already explains the boundary or the oracle is not an adjacent boundary
decision_rules.counterpoint: 1/5 rows remain counterpoints; AgentRewardBench looping is better explained by repeat_signal_change than the learned backend.
decision_rules.evidence: 1 accept, 3 caution, and 1 reject decisions across 5 family rows. Boundary backends beat the best simple baseline on 4/5 tested rows; OSWorld-Human R297 reaches F1 0.7735 versus best baseline 0.7090, and R299 also improves AgentNet quality-state boundaries.
decision_rules.use_when: adjacent-boundary labels are available and learned fields beat simple sequence/field baselines

decision_rules.avoid_when: inspection work is the primary objective and fixed-session is cheaper
decision_rules.counterpoint: Inspection-cost metrics are mixed: top-5 work changes by +0.0813 and first-positive work by +0.1581. Top-5 work delta 0.0813; first-positive work delta 0.1581.
decision_rules.evidence: On held-out OSWorld-Human, learned-boundary fields improve AP 0.2402->0.2583, reduce groups 108->74, and raise top-5 recall by 0.1111. AP gain 0.0181 and group reduction 34.
decision_rules.use_when: visible phase/action fields fail on human-boundary localization
